standard_prerequisites: The Gysin homomorphism attached to a triple of an invertible sheaf, a meromorphic section and its divisor of zeros, and the induced triples obtained by restricting to a divisor and on the intersection

The key formula comparing the two ways of writing the difference of two divisor constructions as a boundary, and the local order bookkeeping in henselized local rings at the generic points of the prime divisors
Rational equivalence for locally finite sums of cycles, which upgrades an equality of cycle representatives produced this way to an equality of rational equivalence classes
core_obligations: Set up the two closed immersions of the intersection of the divisors and observe that the claim is the equality of the two composites applied to a class
Reduce to the class of a single integral closed subspace, since the general case follows from locally finite sums and the shape of the rational equivalences constructed below

Choose meromorphic sections of the two restricted sheaves on that subspace, normalised to agree with the given sections outside the respective divisors, and write the two divisors as locally finite sums weighted by orders

Observe that only those prime divisors that lie inside the respective divisor can occur with nonzero order, choose generating local sections at the henselized local rings and read the two composites as sums weighted by the orders of the corresponding quotients

Apply the key formula to express the difference of the two sums as a sum of boundaries, note that the boundary vanishes at every prime divisor not contained in the intersection of the two divisors, and conclude the rational equivalence
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the class of one integral closed subspace and set up normalised meromorphic sections of the two restricted sheaves
Write both composites as locally finite sums weighted by orders in henselized local rings
Apply the key formula and discard the boundaries that vanish outside the intersection
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the commutativity of two Gysin pullbacks at source lines 3788-3801, label lemma-gysin-commutes-gysin, whose proof occupies source lines 3803-3864. The proof reduces to the class of a single integral closed subspace, then normalises meromorphic sections of the two restricted invertible sheaves so that they agree with the given sections outside the respective divisors, and rewrites each of the two composites as a locally finite sum over prime divisors weighted by orders in the henselizations of the local rings at their generic points. The identification of the two expressions is not immediate, because the two sums are indexed by different divisors; it is the key formula that produces a rational equivalence between them, and the bookkeeping consists in checking that the boundary terms vanish precisely at the prime divisors outside the intersection. The counted statement records none of this.
